_readme: Copy to configs/config.json (or configs/config-<you>.json for a per-person setup — each config automatically pairs with its own states/state-<you>.json) and edit. Every key except "classes" is optional — omitted keys use the defaults shown here, which are already tuned for the fastest polite detection. Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored.
_classes_note: REQUIRED. Add both the LECTURE and your DISCUSSION/LAB section as separate entries: the waitlist only enrolls you if the linked discussion/lab also has an open seat (SIS FAQ #1056), so watch both. Each URL is a section content page from classes.berkeley.edu (open your class, click the specific section, copy the address).
_reserved_groups_note: Who YOU are — majors/minors/programs whose reserved seats you can snipe. Each entry is either text substring-matched (case-insensitive) against a reserved-seat group description ("Statistics" matches "Statistics Majors"; "Computer Science" matches the long EECS/CS/ECE list) or an all-digit requirement-group code matched exactly ("001600" or "1600"). Prefix a token with ! to EXCLUDE blocks it hits even when another token matches — e.g. ["Computer Science", "!Transfer"] skips 'Computer Science Majors: New Transfer Students'. Run  python3 snipe.py --show-reserved  to print your classes' actual groups verbatim and copy from there. Leave empty if none apply — then only unreserved seats count as yours. ("Students with Enrollment Permission" seats are SID-held and never text-match.) Also settable per class inside a classes[] entry.
_alert_on_note: Default: ["eligible"] — ping when the number of open seats YOU can snipe goes up (open unreserved + open reserved for your reserved_groups; with no groups set, just open unreserved). Other triggers: "*" (ANY open-seat increase, reserved included — use this to see everything), "unreserved" (open unreserved seats, snipeable by anyone), "reserved" (open reserved count rises — held for a group, snipeable only if it's yours), "waitlist" (a spot on the waitlist opens up — the waitlist was full and now has room to get in line, not merely the line advancing), "capacity" (max capacity rises — the course was expanded), "status" (status flips to Open). Combine freely, e.g. ["eligible", "waitlist"]. Also settable per class inside a classes[] entry.
_poll_interval_note: Default 60. With fast_poll this is roughly your detection latency. Keep it >= 60 (>= 30 at the very lowest): the fragment endpoint is uncached, so every poll reaches the origin.
_fast_poll_note: Default true. Reads real-time seat/waitlist counts from the UNCACHED associated-sections fragment (/sections/associated/<node>), so detection latency ~= poll_interval_seconds instead of the ~15-min page cache. Probe discovery is automatic; several watched sections of one course share a single fragment request per poll. When the numbers move, the reserved breakdown is fetched from the uncached ajax variant (real-time); full section pages are fetched only every content_refresh_seconds for status + group codes. Set false (or pass --no-fast-poll) for the v0.2 full-page-only behavior.
_content_refresh_note: Default 450. Fast mode only: how often to refresh the full section page for O/W/C status + requirement-group codes. The reserved OPEN counts are read live from the uncached ajax variant on every change, so this only affects the rarely-changing status label and the requirement-group codes; live seat/reserved counts never depend on it.
_bust_cache_note: Default true. Affects FULL-PAGE fetches only (all legacy-mode polls; fast-mode periodic refreshes — the change-triggered reserved fetch uses the always-uncached ajax variant). Pages sit behind a Fastly CDN + Drupal caches (max-age=900); busting appends a unique query param that misses the CDN/edge cache, roughly HALVING page staleness (worst ~30 min -> ~15 min). It does NOT reach real-time: the origin dynamic render cache (~15 min) can't be bypassed from outside — that's what the fragment tier is for.
_alert_pacing_note: Both default 0 (off). alert_cooldown_seconds suppresses a repeat of the same alert kind within N seconds (anti-spam when a seat flickers). repeat_while_open_seconds re-pings every N seconds while seats stay snipeable, so the first alert isn't the only one.

notify._email_note: Copy _email_example to "email" to enable. For the SMTP password use EITHER "password_env" (the NAME of an environment variable) OR an inline "password" (a Gmail App Password works; its whitespace is stripped automatically). If both are set, the inline "password" wins. Inline secrets live in this file in plaintext, so keep config.json out of version control (this project's .gitignore already covers it).
notify._email_to_sms_note: GET ALERTS AS A TEXT: "to" accepts multiple comma-separated recipients, and carriers run free email-to-SMS gateways, so add <your-10-digit-number>@<gateway> to also receive each alert as a text, e.g. "to": "you@berkeley.edu, 5105551234@tmomail.net". Gateways -- T-Mobile (incl. Mint/Metro/Ultra): @tmomail.net; Verizon: @vtext.com (SMS) or @vzwpix.com (MMS); AT&T: @txt.att.net (SMS) or @mms.att.net (MMS); Google Fi: @msg.fi.google.com; Cricket: @sms.cricketwireless.net (SMS) or @mms.cricketwireless.net (MMS). Prefer the MMS gateway when distinct (plain SMS caps ~160 chars and can truncate). A ported/MVNO number may use a different gateway than its original carrier.
notify._telegram_note: Copy _telegram_example to "telegram" to enable. For the bot token use EITHER "bot_token_env" OR an inline "bot_token"; if both are set, the inline token wins. Inline secrets live in this file in plaintext, so keep config.json out of version control.
